comparatorRouteSelection.basis: OER Article 10.2 names three specialisations (Philosophy, Politics, Economics) and Article 11.4 requires every student to follow exactly two of them; the normalized target is the generic bachelor and names no specific pair. All three pairings share an identical60ECofYear1common units plus12ECof sharedYear2Practice and an identical Year-3 structure, and combine exactly two disciplines to the same depth (two compulsory courses per chosen specialisation plus four restricted electives, at least one per chosen track), so no pairing is more representative of the programme's broad academic identity, and none is less specialised, than another under the curriculum page, future page or OER Article 10.1's own symmetric description of the three disciplines. The OER's Appendix 1 (Programme overview) prints exactly three annual-plan tables in a fixed order -- 'TRACKS PHILOSOPHY & ECONOMICS', then 'TRACKS PHILOSOPHY & POLITICAL SCIENCE', then 'TRACKS POLITICAL SCIENCE & ECONOMICS' -- so the official-order tie-break selects the first-listed pairing, Philosophy & Economics, fixed before any UCR course was considered and independent of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The three routes follow VU’s evidenced discipline pairings and change curricular weight substantially. The closest option links advanced philosophy and economics to public choice. The political-economy option prioritises international institutions, law and conflict, while the philosophy-and-politics option links agency and rights to political authority and limits economics to an introduction. All exceed the four-course distinctness floor. Generator rows 5102–5111, 5122, 5123 and 5125 are assigned to the closest route or the political-economy candidate. Career and topic examples 5126–5136 do not justify another option.

notes.text: The UCR options offer different combinations of philosophy, politics and economics. VU has a dedicated Philosophy of Science course and an integrated PPE in Practice sequence. Its supervised tutorial leads to a required 12 EC thesis. Optional UCR independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: VU’s Philosophy, Politics and Economics degree examines social questions through philosophical argument, political analysis and economics. Students begin with all three disciplines, specialise in two and apply their learning in a sequence of interdisciplinary courses. A supervised tutorial prepares them for the required individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three ways to combine these fields: philosophy and economics, political economy and global governance, or philosophy and politics. VU adds a dedicated sequence of interdisciplinary applications, specialist coursework and a compulsory supervised thesis.

curriculum.limitation: This 180 EC route shows one permitted combination of four second-year electives, qualitative research methods and a 30 EC study-abroad package. VU approves the courses taken abroad. Students complete the required earlier credits before starting the tutorial and thesis.
